_comment: Provenance for this package's fixtures. Mirrors ../../codex/testdata/MANIFEST.json's discipline (memory 'silent-no-op-failure-mode': assert on real payload content, never just entry counts) — adapted for a SQLITE-backed vendor store instead of a JSONL one, so there is no single 'rollout file' to shorten; instead one committed JSON document (conversation-fixture.json) captures ONE real conversations_v2 row, and kiro_test.go builds a temporary sqlite db from it at test time via modernc.org/sqlite (CREATE TABLE conversations_v2 + one INSERT) rather than committing a binary .sqlite3 file — keeps the fixture diffable in review and exercises the SAME real INSERT/SELECT round trip a production db would.
real_source_db: ~/.local/share/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3 on the box this package was developed on — the REAL kiro-cli conversation store (confirmed present, inspected READ-ONLY via Python's stdlib sqlite3 module before any Go code was written; never mutated). Not ~/.kiro/ — see schema.go's package doc for why that distinction matters (the deleted v1 reader looked at ~/.kiro/sessions/cli/<id>.jsonl, a file this box's real kiro-cli installs never write).

conversation-fixture.json.real_source: conversations_v2 row for conversation_id 74b27b3b-19e1-41f3-a8a6-bc8e227a3edb (key/workdir /tmp/.../scratchpad/agylive/kirotest), a live kiro-cli oneshot session on this box: a Prompt asking kiro to overwrite a sentinel file, an fs_write ToolUse the local policy layer rejected (CancelledToolUses, status Error), and the assistant's Response explaining the rejection.
conversation-fixture.json.real_fields: conversation_id, EVERY field of both history turns' user.content and assistant (Prompt text, the fs_write tool_uses[0] id/name/args verbatim, the CancelledToolUses rejection prompt text verbatim, the tool_use_results status/content Text verbatim, the Response text verbatim), both request_metadata blocks' request_id/message_id/model_id/chat_conversation_type/timestamps/token fields (every token field really is null on this box — see schema.go's requestMetadata doc comment), and model_info in full.
conversation-fixture.json.trimmed_not_real: request_metadata.time_to_first_chunk and .time_between_chunks — real high-cardinality per-chunk streaming-latency arrays (dozens of {secs,nanos} pairs) this adapter never reads; removed only to keep the fixture reviewable, not because their real values were unavailable. Nothing this adapter actually PARSES was altered.
conversation-fixture.json.created_at / updated_at: the real conversations_v2 column values for this row (Unix ms), copied verbatim into the fixture db's own columns by the test's fixture builder.

golden.transcript.acp.jsonl.provenance: NOT hand-written — generated by running kiro.Adapter{}.Convert against the fixture db built from conversation-fixture.json and capturing the Recorder's output verbatim (see kiro_test.go's TestConvert_MatchesGolden, which re-generates and diffs against this file on every run — a checked-in expectation, not a separately hand-maintained format).
golden.transcript.acp.jsonl.harp/seq/ts: harp and ts are stamped by the test's Recorder construction the same way codex's golden fixture documents (ts reflects wall-clock test-run time, so the comparison zeroes it; seq is deterministic and IS asserted verbatim).

mapping_test.go fixtures.toolResultEvents success-with-text case: copied verbatim from conversations_v2 row for conversation_id 82661ac2-1756-4a0f-a423-8c7358e7660a, history[1].user.content.ToolUseResults (tool_use_id tooluse_EwOLTyvr0mQrXDUUOBlXUi, status Success, content Text 'hello world test file') paired with history[0].assistant.ToolUse's real fs_read tool_uses[0] (same tool_use_id, args {"operations":[{"mode":"Line","path":...}]}) — the one real, non-empty-Text ToolUseResults success case found across every conversation on this box (every other Success result had an empty Text, matching conversation-fixture.json's own ToolUseResults-shaped CancelledToolUses.tool_use_results Error case).
